messages:
maria_ml: Heads up — bringing up a new HF model (llama-ish fork) and the HF generation_config.json layout is tripping our HF->Redwood mapping. reproduction test shows sampling outputs diverge a lot from local HF runs.

maria_ml: minimal generation_config.json from the model repo:
```json
{"temperature": 0.7, "top_k": 0, "top_p": 0.95, "repetition_penalty": 1.1}
```

maria_ml: on HF python, sampling looks like we expect. on Redwood hosted run, tokens are much more repetitive and lower entropy. suspect we’re losing rep_penalty or coercing numeric types to strings somewhere. :thinking_face:

nina_research: hmm — did you check the chat template mapping? some of these models ship a chat template that overrides sampling defaults or injects special tokens.

maria_ml: good call. the model has a chat_template in config.json: "chat_template": "<|user|> {input} <|assistant|>" — we currently parse chat_template into our conversation framing but we also have a conversion step that merges generation_config defaults. possible collision there.

jonathan: can you paste the Redwood-converted params we actually send to runtime? maybe the conversion is dropping `repetition_penalty` when top_k==0 or something silly.

maria_ml: converted payload we observed in logs:
```json
{"temperature": "0.7", "top_k": null, "top_p": "0.95"}
```

maria_ml: notice `repetition_penalty` missing and numeric values are strings. top_k became null because HF uses 0 to mean "disabled" and we convert 0->null. runtime treats null top_k as 0 which is interpreted as "keep all logits" vs our expected fallback of 50.

casey: whoops. numeric stringification will kill fast-path comparisons in runtime (we compare type). I’ve seen this when we json.load a HF config and then run a serializer that coerces via templates.

sam_engineer: quantization experiments exacerbate the issue — int8 sampler is more sensitive to missing rep_penalty. we saw much worse repetition on 8-bit runs vs float32 for the same apparent params.

nina_research: root causes list: (1) chat_template parsing can drop generation defaults when template contains role tokens, (2) 0->null conversion for top_k, (3) numeric->string coercion, (4) missing coercion for `repetition_penalty` if not present in chat-specific overrides.

jonathan: proposed quick fixes:
- treat top_k==0 as explicit "disabled" and convert to `top_k: 0` in payload (do not null it).
- preserve numeric types (float/int) when merging HF generation_config -> Redwood params; add unit test for type preservation.
- if `repetition_penalty` exists anywhere (model config or gen config), ensure it flows to runtime; default to 1.0 if missing.

casey: add a compatibility shim: if top_k is 0 in HF config, map to `top_k: 0` and enforce runtime fallback to a configured default if we want to emulate HF behaviour. Also, add a conversion rule: string->number if looks_like_number.

maria_ml: I can add a small failing integration test (HF repo import -> converted payload) that demonstrates the entropy/regression. will push test and sample model JSON.

deploy-bot: new PR created by maria_ml: `ml/hf-genconfig-preserve-types` — CI: queued. :rocket:

sam_engineer: long-term: add an eval that compares HF python sampling vs Redwood hosted sampling on a fixed seed and prompt set (and quantized variants). flag regressions by KL or repetition rate per 100 tokens.

nina_research: agree — also watch chat-template edgecases: models that embed special tokens like `<|assistant|>` vs role-based lists. our chat conversion currently treats templates as higher priority than generation defaults which is surprising. propose precedence: model.generation_config <- chat_template framing mergers <- runtime overrides.

jonathan: created internal ticket INF-4219 to track: "HF->RW genconfig conversion: types, top_k=0 semantics, rep_penalty propagation, chat_template precedence". Assign to @casey and @maria_ml.

casey: will follow up with a small patch to the converter today, and add a unit test matrix for (top_k:0/50), (top_p missing vs 1.0), (rep_penalty present/absent), (numeric typed vs string).

maria_ml: thanks — once converter is in, I’ll re-run the quantized eval matrix and post KL scores. for now mark the model onboarding as blocked on the conversion fix. :white_check_mark:

sam_engineer: note: we should also add a regression alert that triggers if repetition_rate increases >10% vs HF baseline after conversion — to catch these mapping bugs earlier during onboarding.

maria_ml: agreed. logging the eval plan in the onboarding checklist.

jonathan: nice catch. small bug but big perf/quality delta. :raised_hands:
